TableConverter - Class in com.dfiles.service
Facade for the Convert feature: given raw input bytes, a text encoding, an input format (or TableInputFormat.AUTO to sniff one), and an output format, produces the converted result.
TableData - Record Class in com.dfiles.model
A generic in-memory table — column names plus rows of string cell values — used as the common intermediate form for the Convert feature: every supported input format (CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown table, YAML, XLSX) is parsed into a TableData, and every supported output format (SQL, CSV) is written from one.

TextPreviewService - Class in com.dfiles.service
Reads the first and last N lines of a text file without loading the whole thing into memory — the head comes from a normal line-by-line read that stops early, and the tail comes from seeking near the end of the file and only decoding that trailing chunk.

TsvTableWriter - Class in com.dfiles.service
Renders a TableData as tab-separated text, the same no-quoting convention DelimitedTableParser.parseTsv(java.lang.String) reads back — a cell containing a literal tab or line break isn't escaped, matching how TSV is conventionally produced.

Parses an XML document shaped like repeated records — most commonly the same shape XmlTableWriter produces, e.g.
XmlTableWriter - Class in com.dfiles.service
Renders a TableData as XML — a <table> root containing one <row> per record, each with one child element per column — using the JDK's built-in XMLStreamWriter (StAX) rather than hand-built strings, so text content is always correctly escaped.

YamlTableParser - Class in com.dfiles.service
Parses the one YAML shape that maps naturally onto a table — a sequence of flat mappings, the same "list of records" pattern JSON uses for tabular data:
YamlTableWriter - Class in com.dfiles.service
Renders a TableData as the "list of flat mappings" YAML shape YamlTableParser reads back — one --prefixed block per row, one key: value line per column.
